If you did not need to build a house (or other building) at a site, but could instead build pieces in a factory, what could you do? What materials could you incorporate that would not work well when building vertical walls? (Maybe a material that starts off as a liquid?) How would you transport the pieces from the factory to the building site? Could you create a totally different paradigm for buildings, such as easily reconfigurable rooms? Are there aspects to how buildings are built today that are practical but result in missed opportunities for improving health, comfort, or environmental impact? The challenge is to develop an innovative solution that incorporates substantial changes in building materials or construction methods, leading to benefits such as increased productivity through reduced construction time, new business models or jobs, improvements to worker safety, reduced cost and waste, improvements to occupant comfort and health, and reduced energy use. Other benefits, such as creating flexible interior spaces, can also be a key driver. The solution could include one or more of the following strategies: • The application of a new construction method or material. This method or material does not have to be completely novel; it could be an existing process or material used in other manufacturing sectors. The solution will include details about how this change can be applied to buildings and why it is an improvement over traditional options. • A solution for buildings that will allow rooms to be more easily reconfigured. This can be beneficial during extreme circumstances but will also be beneficial under normal circumstances, such as a fluctuation in the number of on-site employees for commercial buildings or special events. Be sure to consider how heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC); electrical; data; and fire protection will be easily reconfigured with the rooms. • A solution that takes advantage of new construction processes, new materials, or both to substantially improve the functionality of disaster-relief housing in both design and logistics. • A solution focused on building materials, construction methods, or design that promotes recovery, reuse, or recycling of material to eliminate waste and encourage continual use of resources (e.g., design for disassembly and reuse). 2.2 Indoor Environmental Quality Indoor environmental quality is the combined impact of indoor air quality (IAQ), thermal comfort, lighting, and acoustics (Gudeman 2020).
